l.i: Sed demus[?] miseras illas anus posse grandine producere, at id non possunt, nisi permittente & puniente Deo peccata nostra: His, vera poenitentia, sublatis, sublata est causa, nec praeterea timendae sunt sagae.

Fit etiā interdum, vt propter continuos imbres, & pluuias fruges magna ex parte pereant, nec satis commodè colligi possint. Quae etiam egestatis causa esse[?]. Fruges etiam ad falcem maturae conteri, aut ab hostibus demeti, vel exuri possunt. Sic Samson caudibus vulpinis, faces ardentes alligauit, & Philistinorum sata perdidit.

Etsi verò fruges repositae sint in horrea, & vina in cellas conuecta, fit tamen vt laboribus etiam maligne respondeant. In trituratione[?], in furno, in caniftro maledictio Domini sentitur:hac de re audiuntur crebrae agricolarum querelae. Item horrea plena frumenti fulmine tacta, vel alio incendio, pereunt: Vina in dolio accessunt vapescūt, aut alia vitia contrahūt, saepe effluunt. Nihil dicam quod hostes omne frumentum consumunt, hortos & granaria igne vastant: cados vini confringunt, gunt,

page.notes: Uncertain readings: "demus" in the first line (possibly "demum"); "esse" in "egestatis causa esse" is written as a stylised abbreviation; "trituratione" is broken across the line end with no printed hyphen, so it is written whole and marked [?]. "accessunt" keeps the long s as s in the source only where it is printed; written here as printed. The last line "gunt," is the continuation of "confringunt" after the hyphen at the line end, so the paragraph is joined. The word "anus" is printed as is.
